The local factors are the usual Weil-Deligne root numbers at finite places, equal to1 at all but finitely many places, and -1 at every archimedean place; their definition does not assume analytic continuation of L(E/K,s).

records.title: Global Existence of Classical Solutions to the Relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell System
records.exactTarget: Prove or disprove that the Cauchy problem for the three-dimensional relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell system has a global classical solution (f,E,B) for every sufficiently regular finite-energy initial datum.

records.title: Artin's primitive root conjecture
records.exactTarget: Prove or disprove that every integer a other than -1 that is not a perfect square is a primitive root modulo p for a positive natural density of primes p, with the density given by Artin's predicted correction factor.

records.title: Falconer distance set conjecture
records.exactTarget: Prove or disprove that for every integer d>=2 and every compact set E in R^d with Hausdorff dimension greater than d/2, the distance set Delta(E)={|x-y|: x,y in E} has positive one-dimensional Lebesgue measure.

records.title: Hopf conjecture for positive sectional curvature
records.exactTarget: Prove that every closed even-dimensional Riemannian manifold whose sectional curvatures are everywhere positive has positive Euler characteristic.

records.title: Local Smoothing Conjecture for Wave Equations
records.exactTarget: For every n >= 3, p > 2n/(n-1), and epsilon > 0, prove ||exp(it sqrt(-Delta))f||_{L^p(R^n x [1,2])} <= C_{p,epsilon} ||f||_{W^{s_p-1/p+epsilon,p}(R^n)}, where s_p=(n-1)(1/2-1/p).

records.title: Hilbert-Smith Conjecture
records.exactTarget: Prove that every locally compact topological group acting faithfully on a connected topological manifold is a Lie group; equivalently, prove that Z_p admits no faithful action by homeomorphisms on a connected manifold.

records.title: Grothendieck–Serre Conjecture on Principal Bundles over Regular Local Rings
records.exactTarget: For every commutative Noetherian regular local ring R, with fraction field K=Frac(R), and every reductive R-group scheme G (smooth affine with connected reductive geometric fibers), every G-torsor over Spec(R) that becomes trivial over Spec(K) is already trivial over Spec(R). Equivalently, the natural map of nonabelian pointed sets H^1_et(R,G) -> H^1_et(K,G) has trivial kernel. Regular local rings here are domains. No field-containing, excellence, finite-type, unramified, quasi-split, isotropic or constant-group restriction is imposed.

records.title: Kimura–O'Sullivan Finite-Dimensionality Conjecture
records.exactTarget: For every field k and every smooth projective variety X over k, the Chow motive h(X) with rational coefficients in the ordinary symmetric, pseudo-abelian category CHM(k)_Q is Kimura–O'Sullivan finite-dimensional: there exist motives M+ and M− and positive integers n,m such that h(X) is isomorphic to M+ direct-sum M−, the exterior power Λ^n(M+) is zero, and the symmetric power Sym^m(M−) is zero. The summands may be zero. The field k is unrestricted; characteristic zero applies to the rational coefficient field, not to k. No effective construction, uniform n,m or classification is required.

records.title: Exact Asymptotic Waring Function G(k)
records.exactTarget: For each integer k>=3, let G(k) be the least positive integer s for which every sufficiently large positive integer N is expressible as a sum of at most s positive integral k-th powers. Determine the entire function G(k) for all k>=3. Equivalently, zeros may be allowed and exactly s nonnegative integral k-th powers used; this is not the condition of exactly s positive summands.

records.title: Rank One Abelian Stark Conjecture
records.exactTarget: Let K/F be an abelian extension of number fields with Galois group G, and let S be a finite set of places of F containing the archimedean and ramified places, with |S| >= 2 and at least one place v of S splitting completely in K. Prove that, for a fixed place w of K above v, there exists a unit u in U_{v,S} such that zeta'_{K/F,S}(sigma, 0) = -(1/e) log |u^sigma|_w for all sigma in G, where e is the number of roots of unity in K, and K(u^{1/e})/F is abelian.

records.title: Long-Range Order in the Quantum Heisenberg Ferromagnet
records.exactTarget: For the nearest-neighbor isotropic spin-S quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet on Z^d with Hamiltonian H=-sum_{<x,y>} S_x dot S_y, assert: for every integer d>=3 and every S in{1/2,1,3/2,...}, there is a finite beta_0(d,S)>0 such that for each finite beta>=beta_0 the infinite-volume zero-field model admits a translation-invariant equilibrium Gibbs state with nonzero spin expectation. Nonzero expectation refers to spontaneous magnetization in a symmetry-breaking state, not the rotation-invariant mixture. Coupling J=1 fixes temperature units; no pointwise-correlation equivalence is asserted.

records.title: Kaplansky's Zero-Divisor Conjecture for Torsion-Free Groups
records.exactTarget: Prove that for every torsion-free group G and every field K, the group ring K[G] has no non-trivial zero-divisors, i.e. K[G] is a domain.

records.title: Effective Roth Theorem
records.witness: effective Roth
records.exactTarget: There exists one total computable algorithm which, given a real algebraic irrational alpha by its integer minimal polynomial and a rational isolating interval, and a positive rational epsilon, returns an integer Q>=1 such that every reduced rational p/q, with p an integer and q>=1 an integer, satisfying |alpha-p/q|<q^(-2-epsilon) has q<=Q. The algorithm must halt with this guarantee on every valid input. No time, space, practical-size or software-implementation requirement is imposed.

records.title: Serre's Conjecture II on Galois Cohomology of Simply Connected Semisimple Groups
records.exactTarget: Let K be a perfect field of cohomological dimension at most 2. Prove that every principal homogeneous space under a semisimple simply connected linear algebraic K-group has a rational point, i.e. H^1(K,G) = 1 for every such group G.

records.title: Polynomial-Time Quantum Algorithm for the Dihedral Hidden Subgroup Problem
records.exactTarget: Find a polynomial-time quantum algorithm with poly(log N) operations and space for the hidden subgroup problem in dihedral groups D_N.

records.title: Breuil-Mezard conjecture: equality of the Galois and automorphic sides
records.exactTarget: Conjecture (Breuil-Mezard): the equality sigma_Gal = sigma_Aut holds, where sigma_Gal and sigma_Aut are the Galois and automorphic (locally algebraic) representations attached to a mod p Galois representation.

records.title: Polynomial Diameter Bound for Polytopes
records.exactTarget: Prove or disprove that there is a polynomial p such that the vertex-edge graph of every pointed d-dimensional polyhedron, bounded or unbounded, with n facets has diameter at most p(n,d).

records.title: Density of Hyperbolicity for Complex Polynomials
records.exactTarget: For each complex polynomial T of degree at least two, determine whether T can be approximated by polynomials of the same degree all of whose critical points converge under iteration to attracting periodic cycles, that is, whether hyperbolic polynomials are dense in the space of complex polynomials of each degree.

records.title: Palis finite-attractor full-basin density conjecture
records.exactTarget: For every compact connected boundaryless smooth manifold M and every finite integer r >= 1, prove the conjunction of the following two density assertions: (i) in Diff^r(M) with its C^r topology there is a dense subset D whose elements f have finitely many attractors whose basins of attraction together cover M up to a set of smooth-volume measure zero; (ii) the same holds in the space X^r(M) of C^r vector fields with its C^r topology, for the attractors and basins of the generated flows. Attractor follows Palis (2005) Sections 2.1 and 2.3: a compact invariant set A that is transitive (has a dense orbit) and attracts a set of positive volume, its basin being the set of points whose forward orbit (or forward flow trajectory) converges to A. The finite number of attractors may depend on the element of D; no uniform bound is required. Volume-zero is independent of the choice of smooth positive density on M. This is the first bullet of Palis's Global Conjecture only; physical measures, stochastic stability, metric stability under parameter perturbation, and one-dimensional-family statements are separate conjectures not included.

records.title: Sharp Erdos Distinct-Distances Conjecture in the Plane
records.exactTarget: Let D(n) be the minimum, over all sets of n distinct points in the Euclidean plane, of the number of distinct pairwise distances determined by the set. Prove D(n) = Omega(n/sqrt(log n)), matching up to a constant factor the square-lattice construction D(n) = O(n/sqrt(log n)).

records.title: Brauer-Manin obstruction for number-field curves: Hasse-principle form
records.exactTarget: For every number field k and every smooth projective geometrically connected curve C/k of genus at least two, if C(A_k)^Br is nonempty then C(k) is nonempty. Here Br(C)=H^2_et(C,G_m) is the full cohomological Brauer group, and C(A_k)^Br consists of adelic tuples (P_v) for which sum_v inv_v(alpha(P_v))=0 for every alpha in Br(C). Constants obey global reciprocity. Passing at archimedean places to connected components does not change nonemptiness. No rational base point, degree-one divisor class, Sha finiteness, rank bound or effective Jacobian presentation is assumed.

records.title: Skolem Problem for Linear Recurrence Sequences
records.witness: the Skolem problem
records.exactTarget: Decide algorithmically, given an integer (or algebraic) linear recurrence sequence, whether it has a zero term.

records.title: Morton–Silverman Uniform Boundedness Conjecture
records.exactTarget: For all fixed integers N>=1, d>=2 and D>=1, there exists a finite constant C(N,d,D) such that for every number field K with [K:Q]<=D and every degree-d K-morphism phi:P^N_K->P^N_K, the set of K-rational preperiodic points has cardinality at most C(N,d,D). A point is preperiodic when its forward orbit under phi is finite. The morphism is everywhere defined, equivalently given by homogeneous degree-d forms with no common projective zero. The bound is independent of the field and map except for N,d,D; no effective formula or classification is required.

records.title: Parshin Conjecture on Higher K-Theory over Finite Fields
records.exactTarget: Prove that for every smooth projective variety X over a finite field and every integer n greater than zero, the higher algebraic K-group K_n(X) is torsion.

records.title: De Giorgi Conjecture for the Allen-Cahn Equation in Dimensions 4 to 8
records.exactTarget: For each ambient dimension N with 4 <= N <= 8, prove that every bounded entire C^2 solution u from R^N to (-1,1) of the Allen-Cahn equation Laplacian u = u^3 - u that is strictly monotone in one direction is one-dimensional, that is, u(x) = g(a . x) for some unit vector a and one-variable profile g.

records.title: Moonshine Uniqueness Conjecture (Strongly Rational Holomorphic VOA Form)
records.exactTarget: Every strongly rational, holomorphic vertex operator algebra V of central charge 24 with V_1=0 is isomorphic to the moonshine vertex operator algebra V-natural. Here strongly rational means simple, of CFT type (V=sum_{n>=0} V_n and V_0=C1), self-contragredient, C_2-cofinite, and rational in the sense that every admissible V-module is completely reducible; holomorphic means that V is the only irreducible V-module up to isomorphism in this rational setting.

records.title: All-Pairs Shortest Paths in Truly Subcubic Time
records.exactTarget: Determine whether exact all-pairs shortest paths on weighted n-vertex graphs can be computed in O(n^(3-epsilon)) time for some fixed epsilon greater than zero.

records.title: UCT Problem for Separable Nuclear Complex C*-Algebras
records.exactTarget: Decide whether EVERY separable nuclear complex C*-algebra A, unital or nonunital, satisfies the Rosenberg-Schochet UCT: for EVERY separable complex C*-algebra B, unital or nonunital, and each j in Z/2, the canonical UCT sequence 0 -> E_j(A,B) -> KK_j(A,B) -> H_j(A,B) -> 0 is exact. Here H_j(A,B)=direct_sum_(i=0,1) Hom_Z(K_i(A),K_(i+j)(B)) and E_j(A,B)=direct_sum_(i=0,1) Ext_Z^1(K_i(A),K_(i+j+1)(B)), with indices modulo2. The right map is the natural map on K-theory induced by KK classes; the left is the canonical inverse extension-class identification of the kernel, not an arbitrary chosen injection. No canonical or natural splitting is required. Equivalently, every such A belongs to the Rosenberg-Schochet bootstrap category of separable nuclear C*-algebras, or is KK-equivalent to a separable commutative complex C*-algebra.

records.title: Shub-Smale τ-Conjecture for Integer Zeros
records.exactTarget: Determine whether universal constants a > 0 and c >= 1 exist such that every nonzero polynomial f in Z[x] has at most a(1 + tau(f))^c distinct integer zeros, where tau(f) is the shortest constant-free straight-line-program length using addition, subtraction, and multiplication, starting from 1 and x.

records.title: Polynomial-Time Distribution-Free PAC Learning of DNF Formulas
records.exactTarget: Given an unknown s-term DNF f on {0,1}^n and random labeled examples drawn from an arbitrary unknown distribution D, construct a possibly improper hypothesis in time polynomial in n, s, 1/epsilon, and log(1/delta) whose D-error is at most epsilon with probability at least 1-delta.

records.title: Exact satisfiability threshold for random k-SAT for small k (k = 3)
records.exactTarget: In the uniform random 3-SAT model, choose a 3-CNF formula with n variables and m clauses uniformly from formulas whose clauses contain three distinct literals. Determine the exact constant r_3 such that, as n tends to infinity with m/n tending to r, satisfiability has probability tending to 1 for r < r_3 and tending to 0 for r > r_3.

records.title: Equidistribution of Galois Orbits of Special Points on Shimura Varieties
records.exactTarget: For any sequence of special points on a Shimura variety that is eventually outside each proper special subvariety of the ambient variety, prove that its finite Galois orbits equidistribute with respect to normalized Haar measure. The qualification is pointwise in the subvariety: each fixed proper special subvariety contains only finitely many terms.

records.title: Vaught's conjecture
records.exactTarget: Prove or disprove that for every complete theory T in a countable first-order language, the number I(T,aleph_0) of pairwise nonisomorphic countable models of T is either at most countable or exactly 2^{aleph_0}.

records.title: 11/8-Conjecture on intersection forms of spin 4-manifolds
records.exactTarget: Prove that every smooth closed oriented spin 4-manifold M satisfies b2(M) >= (11/8)|sigma(M)|.

records.title: Hopf conjecture for nonnegative sectional curvature
records.exactTarget: Prove that every closed even-dimensional Riemannian manifold whose sectional curvatures are everywhere nonnegative has nonnegative Euler characteristic.

records.title: Kawamata's K-Equivalence Implies D-Equivalence Conjecture
records.exactTarget: Let X and Y be smooth projective complex varieties. If a common smooth variety Z has projective birational morphisms f:Z→X and g:Z→Y with f^*K_X linearly equivalent to g^*K_Y, prove an exact equivalence DbCoh(X)≃DbCoh(Y) of triangulated categories.

records.title: Wall's Poincare Duality Group Conjecture
records.exactTarget: For every n≥3 and every finitely presented integral Poincaré duality group G of dimension n, prove that there is a closed aspherical topological n-manifold M with π1(M)≅G and matching orientation character.

records.title: Quantum versus Classical Communication Complexity of Total Functions
records.exactTarget: Prove that for every total Boolean function in the two-party communication model, its bounded-error randomized communication complexity is bounded by a polynomial in its bounded-error quantum communication complexity.

records.title: Berry random-wave conjecture: real negative-curvature BS formulation
records.exactTarget: For every closed connected smooth Riemannian manifold (M,g) of dimension d>=2 with everywhere strictly negative sectional curvature, put mu=dvol_g/vol_g(M). For any real orthonormal eigenbasis of L2(M,mu) for the positive Laplace-Beltrami operator, order the eigenvalues nondecreasingly and omit the finite zero-eigenspace; write Delta_g phi_j=alpha_j^2 phi_j with alpha_j>0. If p is sampled with law mu, does the law of the pointed real-decorated manifold [M,alpha_j^2 g,p,phi_j] converge weakly, along the full positive-energy sequence, in Abert-Bergeron-Le Masson's local smooth topology on pointed isometry classes of real-decorated d-manifolds, to the law of [R^d,g_Euclidean,0,F]? Here F is the centered real stationary isotropic Gaussian field with covariance E[F(x)F(y)]=integral_{S^{d-1}} cos(<x-y,theta>) d sigma(theta), where sigma is probability surface measure on the unit sphere (unit variance and unit spectral radius, no extra 2*pi factor).

records.title: Shafarevich Freeness Conjecture over Qab
records.exactTarget: Let Qab be the maximal abelian extension of Q in an algebraic closure Qbar (equivalently the maximal cyclotomic extension). The absolute Galois group Gal(Qbar/Qab) is a free profinite group of countably infinite rank, in the standard profinite convention of a free basis converging to the identity.

records.title: Kadison Similarity Problem for C*-Algebras
records.exactTarget: Prove or disprove whether every bounded representation of a C*-algebra on a Hilbert space is similar to a *-representation.

records.title: Banach-Mazur Rotation Problem
records.exactTarget: Let X be an infinite-dimensional separable real Banach space whose group of surjective linear isometries acts transitively on the unit sphere. Prove that X is linearly isometric to a Hilbert space, or construct a separable non-Hilbert counterexample.

records.title: Serre Uniformity Question
records.exactTarget: Determine whether there exists a bound N > 0 such that for every non-CM elliptic curve E over Q and every prime p > N, the residual Galois representation rho_{E,p} on E[p] is surjective onto GL_2(F_p).

records.title: The k-Server Conjecture for General Metric Spaces
records.exactTarget: For every integer k >= 1 and every metric space, prove that there is a deterministic online k-server algorithm whose movement cost on every request sequence is at most k times the offline optimum, up to an additive constant.

records.title: Zauner's Conjecture: Unrestricted Complex SIC Existence in Every Dimension
records.witness: d^2 vectors with |<vi,vj>|^2=1/(d+1); exact algebraic SICs are known
records.exactTarget: Decide whether for EVERY integer d>=2 there exist d^2 unit vectors v_1,...,v_(d^2) in the standard complex Hilbert space C^d with |<v_i,v_j>|^2=1/(d+1) whenever i!=j. Their complex lines are distinct. Equivalently, their rank-one projectors P_i=v_i v_i^* have sum_i P_i=d I_d and define SIC-POVM elements M_i=P_i/d; for i!=j the normalized trace is Tr(M_i M_j)=1/[d^2(d+1)]. No Weyl-Heisenberg covariance, order-three symmetry, explicit coordinates or uniform construction algorithm is imposed.

records.title: Perfect-Matching Search in Deterministic NC (General Graphs)
records.witness: perfect matching in deterministic NC
records.exactTarget: Assert the existence of one logspace-uniform family (C_n) of deterministic Boolean AND/OR/NOT circuits which, for every n>=1 and every finite simple undirected graph G on labelled vertices 1,...,n given by its n-by-n adjacency matrix, outputs a perfect matching of G if one exists and outputs a distinguished NO flag if none exists. Matching output is an n-by-n edge-indicator matrix, required to encode disjoint edges covering every vertex and belonging to G; its bits are ignored when NO is output. Circuit size is bounded by C n^c and depth by C (log(n+2))^k for constants C,c,k independent of n and G, and AND/OR fan-in is at most two. A deterministic logspace transducer on unary 1^n outputs the complete circuit description, including all designated outputs. This fixes ordinary logspace-uniform NC for the multi-output search relation. It does not conflate a search algorithm with an unweighted decision algorithm or restrict the input to bipartite or planar graphs.

records.title: Babai's diameter conjecture for nonabelian finite simple groups
records.exactTarget: Is there an absolute constant c>0 such that for every nonabelian finite simple group G and every generating set X of G, the undirected Cayley graph with steps X union X^{-1} has diameter at most (ln |G|)^c? Thus every element of G is a word of that length in X and its inverses, with the same c for all groups and generating sets.

records.title: Chromatic Number of the Plane (Hadwiger-Nelson Problem)
records.exactTarget: Determine the chromatic number of the plane: the minimum number of colors needed to color every point of the Euclidean plane so that any two points at Euclidean distance exactly 1 receive distinct colors.

records.title: Existence of an odd perfect number
records.witness: an odd N with sigma(N)=2N; the divisor sum is checkable
records.exactTarget: Determine whether there exists an odd positive integer N satisfying sigma(N)=2N, where sigma is the sum-of-positive-divisors function; equivalently, prove that every perfect number is even or construct an odd perfect number.

records.title: Dirichlet Divisor Problem
records.exactTarget: Determine the sharp order of the error term Delta(x) in the asymptotic sum_{n<=x} d(n) = x log x + (2 gamma - 1) x + Delta(x) for the summatory divisor function; in particular, prove or disprove that Delta(x) = O(x^(1/4+eps)) for every eps > 0.

records.title: Virasoro Conjecture for Gromov–Witten Invariants
records.exactTarget: For every smooth projective complex variety X, let Z_X be its total descendant Gromov–Witten potential in all genera and curve classes over the Novikov ring. For every integer k>=-1, the Eguchi–Hori–Xiong–Katz Virasoro operator L_k^X, with the conventions and formula of Getzler Section 1.4, annihilates Z_X: L_k^X Z_X=0, coefficient by coefficient, including the graded conventions for odd cohomology.

records.title: Gauss Circle Problem
records.exactTarget: Determine the sharp order of the error term E(r) in N(r) = pi*r^2 + E(r), where N(r) counts the integer lattice points in the disk of radius r centered at the origin; in particular, prove or disprove that E(r) = O(r^(1/2+eps)) for every eps > 0.

records.title: The Singer Conjecture on Vanishing of L2-Cohomology of Aspherical Manifolds
records.exactTarget: Prove that for every closed aspherical n-manifold, all L2-Betti numbers vanish outside degree n/2; in particular, prove that all L2-Betti numbers vanish when n is odd.

records.title: K(pi,1) conjecture for Artin groups
records.exactTarget: For every Coxeter system (W,S) with S finite and arbitrary Coxeter labels, let A_(W,S) be the associated Artin group and X_(W,S) its quotient Salvetti CW complex, with one |T|-cell for each T subset of S whose parabolic group W_T is finite and the standard attaching maps in Paolini Theorem 3.3 or Boyd's Salvetti construction modulo W. Prove that X_(W,S) is aspherical, hence a K(A_(W,S),1). Equivalently, prove the Deligne complex of cosets aA_T with W_T finite, ordered by inclusion, contractible. If an arrangement model is used, it is the W-quotient of the reflection-arrangement complement restricted using the interior of the Tits cone as in those sources, not an unrestricted complexified arrangement for infinite W. No spherical, affine, FC or other diagram-type restriction is imposed on W.

records.title: Infinitude of Mersenne Primes
records.exactTarget: Prove or disprove that there are infinitely many primes p for which the Mersenne number 2^p - 1 is prime. Equivalently (by the Euclid-Euler theorem), prove or disprove that there are infinitely many even perfect numbers.

records.title: Zagier's dimension conjecture for classical multiple zeta values
records.exactTarget: For positive integers k_1,...,k_r with k_1>=2, define the classical convergent real multiple zeta value zeta(k_1,...,k_r)=sum_(n_1>...>n_r>0) 1/(n_1^k_1 ... n_r^k_r), of weight k_1+...+k_r. For each k>=2 let Z_k be their Q-linear span at weight k, with Z_0=Q generated by the empty value1 and Z_1={0}. Define d_0=1,d_1=0,d_2=1 and d_k=d_(k-2)+d_(k-3) for k>=3. Is dim_Q Z_k=d_k for every k>=0?

records.title: Constant-Query Locally Decodable Codes with Polynomial Blocklength
records.witness: constant-query locally decodable codes
records.exactTarget: Construct binary codes of blocklength polynomial in the message length that permit recovery of any message bit with a constant number of queries from words corrupted in a constant fraction of positions, or prove that no such family exists.

records.title: Universal Optimality of the Hexagonal Lattice in Dimension Two
records.exactTarget: Let A2 be the triangular lattice scaled to density1 in R^2. A configuration C is a discrete closed subset with lim(R->infinity)|C intersect B_R(0)|/area(B_R(0))=1. For p(r)=f(r^2), where f:(0,infinity)->R is C-infinity and (-1)^k f^(k)>=0 for every integer k>=0, define lower energy by liminf(R->infinity) |C intersect B_R|^(-1) sum_{x,y in C intersect B_R,x!=y} p(|x-y|), allowing +infinity. Assertion: for every such f and C, this lower energy is at least the corresponding lattice energy E_p(A2), defined by the limit of the same averages (extended values allowed).

records.title: RL versus L
records.exactTarget: Let L be the languages of binary strings decided by deterministic Turing machines using O(log(N+2)) work space on length-N inputs. Let RL use the same read-only input and read-write work-tape convention but allow fresh unbiased read-once random bits, retaining an old bit only by storing it in counted work space. The machine must halt for every input and every random tape, use O(log(N+2)) work space, accept each yes input with probability at least2/3, and accept each no input with probability0. Is every language in RL in L, equivalently RL=L?

records.title: All groups are good: the four-dimensional disc-embedding conjecture
records.exactTarget: Every group Gamma is good in the four-dimensional disc-embedding sense: for every based height1.5 disc-like capped grope G^c (with its standard smooth four-dimensional thickening and framed attaching region) and every homomorphism phi:pi_1(G^c)->Gamma, there exists an immersed disc D->G^c whose framed boundary coincides with that attaching region and whose double-point loops, based by paths in G^c, all map to the identity under phi. The universal assertion is equivalently goodness of the rank-two free group F2, and equivalently goodness of every finitely presented group. Its disc-embedding consequence is in the locally flat topological category, not arbitrary smooth disc embedding.

records.title: Shafarevich Holomorphic-Convexity Conjecture
records.exactTarget: For every connected smooth complex projective variety X, its universal covering complex manifold X-tilde is holomorphically convex: for every compact K contained in X-tilde, the set {z in X-tilde: |f(z)|<=sup_{w in K}|f(w)| for every global holomorphic function f on X-tilde} is compact. This is the classical universal-cover conjecture, not the stronger assertion that X-tilde is Stein and not a statement restricted to linear fundamental groups.

records.title: Dynamical Mordell–Lang Conjecture
records.exactTarget: For every field K of characteristic zero, every quasiprojective variety X over K, every K-morphism f:X->X, every closed K-subvariety V of X and every point x in X(K), the set {n in Z_{≥0}: f^n(x) is in V(K)} is a finite union of arithmetic progressions {a+bm:m in Z_{≥0}} with a,b nonnegative integers. A zero step b=0 permits a singleton, and an empty union permits no returns. All iterates are defined because f is a morphism. No dominance, etaleness, smoothness, automorphism or degree restriction is imposed.

records.title: Witten's Asymptotic Expansion Conjecture for SU(2) WRT Invariants
records.exactTarget: For every closed oriented three-manifold Y, let WRT_k(Y) be the SU(2) Witten-Reshetikhin-Turaev invariant at level k-2 in the standard compact-gauge normalization WRT_k(S^3)=1. For every value S in CS(Y), the set of Chern-Simons actions modulo Z of flat SU(2) connections, there should exist a formal Puiseux Laurent series W_S(tau) in union_{n>=1} C((tau^(1/n))) such that WRT_k(Y) ~ sum_{S in CS(Y)} exp(2*pi*i*k*S) W_S(1/k) as integer k tends to infinity, as a full Poincare asymptotic expansion. The separately named growth-rate and explicit leading-coefficient conjectures are not additional requirements.

records.title: Morrison-Kawamata Cone Conjecture
records.exactTarget: For every projective Q-factorial klt pair (X, Delta) over the complex numbers with K_X + Delta numerically trivial, prove both that Aut(X, Delta) acting on the effective nef cone Nef^e(X) and that PsAut(X, Delta) acting on the effective movable cone Mov^e(X) have rational polyhedral fundamental domains.

records.title: Anosov Diffeomorphism Classification Conjecture
records.exactTarget: Prove that every Anosov diffeomorphism is topologically conjugate to a hyperbolic automorphism of an infranilmanifold.

records.title: Michel Boundary Rigidity Conjecture for Simple Manifolds
records.exactTarget: Let M be a compact smooth manifold with nonempty boundary of dimension n>=3, and g,g' smooth simple Riemannian metrics: the boundary is strictly convex, every two points are joined by a unique geodesic, and there are no conjugate points. Assert that whenever d_g(x,y)=d_g'(x,y) for all boundary points x,y, there exists a diffeomorphism phi:M->M equal to the identity pointwise on the boundary with g'=phi^*g.

records.title: Sidorenko Conjecture on Bipartite Homomorphism Densities
records.witness: a finite H plus a rational step graphon refutes the inequality
records.exactTarget: Prove that for every bipartite graph H and every graphon W, t(H,W) >= t(K_2,W)^{|E(H)|}; equivalently, quasirandom graphs minimize H-homomorphism density at fixed edge density.

records.title: Fermat-Catalan Conjecture on Finiteness of Coprime Power Triples
records.exactTarget: Prove that there are only finitely many pairwise coprime positive-integer triples (x,y,z) for which x^p + y^q = z^r for integers p,q,r > 1 satisfying 1/p + 1/q + 1/r < 1.

records.title: Polynomial-Time Decidability of Semidefinite Programming Feasibility
records.witness: SDP feasibility in P
records.exactTarget: Determine whether feasibility of a semidefinite program with rational symmetric input matrices can be decided in polynomial time in the Turing bit model.

records.title: Resolvent Degree of the General Degree-Seven Polynomial (Algebraic Form of Hilbert's Thirteenth Problem)
records.exactTarget: Prove that the resolvent degree rd_C(7) of the general degree-seven polynomial equals 3; equivalently, establish the lower bound rd_C(7) > 2.

records.title: Classical Worst-Case Hardness Reduction for LWE
records.exactTarget: Determine whether there is a classical (non-quantum) worst-case hardness reduction for the Learning With Errors problem that fully subsumes Regev's quantum reduction, i.e. reducing both GapSVP_gamma and SIVP_gamma to LWE for the same parameters, with polynomial modulus and no loss in lattice dimension.

records.title: Sharp Upper Bound in Yau's Conjecture on Nodal Sets of Laplace Eigenfunctions
records.exactTarget: For every smooth closed n-dimensional Riemannian manifold M with n >= 2, prove that every Laplace eigenfunction phi_lambda satisfying Delta phi_lambda + lambda phi_lambda = 0 obeys H^{n-1}({phi_lambda = 0}) <= C sqrt(lambda), where C depends only on M and its metric.

records.title: MAJORITY is not in ACC0
records.exactTarget: Let MAJORITY_n(x)=1 exactly when sum_i x_i>=n/2. Define nonuniform ACC0 as Boolean families computed, for every input length n>=1, by circuits of polynomial size and some fixed constant depth using unbounded-fan-in AND, OR and MOD_m gates and fan-in-one NOT gates, with constants allowed and one fixed integer modulus m>=2 across all lengths; MOD_m outputs1 exactly when the input sum is divisible by m. Size counts input and internal gates; depth counts gate layers. The depth, modulus and polynomial size bound may depend on the family, not on n. Is the family (MAJORITY_n) outside ACC0?

records.title: Cartan-Hadamard isoperimetric conjecture
records.exactTarget: Prove that every bounded finite-perimeter region in every n-dimensional Cartan-Hadamard manifold satisfies the Euclidean isoperimetric inequality, with equality only for Euclidean balls; equivalently, extend the classical Euclidean isoperimetric lower bound to all complete simply connected Riemannian manifolds of nonpositive sectional curvature.

records.title: Global Regularity of the 2D Inviscid Boussinesq Equations
records.exactTarget: Determine whether all smooth, finite-energy solutions of the two-dimensional inviscid Boussinesq equations (velocity coupled to a temperature or density by buoyancy, without dissipation) on R^2 remain smooth for all time, or whether finite-time singularity formation occurs for some C^infinity initial data; finite-time blow-up is known for some data on domains with corners and near half-space type domains.

records.title: Existence of NPT Bound Entanglement
records.exactTarget: Prove or disprove that there exists a bipartite entangled state with negative partial transpose that is nevertheless undistillable under LOCC.

records.title: Nearby Lagrangian Conjecture
records.exactTarget: Prove that every closed exact Lagrangian submanifold of the cotangent bundle T^*N is Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section N.

records.title: Equivalence or Strict Containment of QMA and QMA(2)
records.exactTarget: Determine whether QMA(2)=QMA in the ordinary unrelativized, uniform polynomial-time quantum verification model. For a promise problem (Y,N), QMA(2) allows two polynomial-size quantum witnesses, required to be a product across the two prover registers: each YES input has some such witness accepted with probability at least 2/3, and each NO input is accepted with probability at most 1/3 for every such witness. QMA allows one unrestricted polynomial-size quantum witness with the same bounds. There is no requirement outside the promise. The verifier uses a fixed standard universal quantum computation model, with no oracle or advice. The two complete outcomes are equality and strict containment QMA properly contained in QMA(2).

records.title: Sample Compression Conjecture (Linear Size in VC Dimension)
records.exactTarget: Prove or disprove that every concept class of finite VC dimension d admits a sample compression scheme of size O(d): any realizable labeled sample can be summarized by O(d) examples plus bounded side information from which a hypothesis consistent with the full sample is reconstructed.

records.title: Mahler Conjecture on the Volume Product of a Convex Body
records.exactTarget: Prove that the product of the volume of a centrally symmetric convex body K in R^n and the volume of its polar body is at least 4^n/n!, with equality attained by the cube (and its polar).

records.title: Kuznetsov Rationality Conjecture for Cubic Fourfolds
records.exactTarget: For every smooth cubic fourfold X contained in P^5_C, let Ku(X) be the full right-orthogonal subcategory of D^b(coh X) consisting of objects E with Hom(O_X(i),E[j])=0 for i=0,1,2 and all integers j. The Kuznetsov rationality conjecture asserts: X is rational, meaning birational over C to P^4_C, if and only if there exists a smooth projective complex K3 surface S and an exact C-linear triangulated equivalence Ku(X) ~= D^b(coh S). The K3 category is untwisted: no nonzero chosen Brauer twist is permitted; this does not require Br(S)=0. No polarization, marking, chosen kernel, explicit algorithm or separately imposed Fourier-Mukai condition is added. The assertion quantifies over ALL smooth complex cubic fourfolds, not only general points of a special divisor.

records.title: Kummer-Vandiver Conjecture on Cyclotomic Class Numbers
records.witness: one prime p with p | h+(Q(zeta_p))
records.exactTarget: Prove that the prime p does not divide the class number h+(Q(zeta_p)) of the maximal real subfield of the p-th cyclotomic field for all primes p.

records.title: Secret key from all entangled states
records.exactTarget: Determine whether every bipartite entangled quantum state rho has strictly positive distillable secret key K_D(rho) under asymptotic local operations and public classical communication.

records.title: Frey-Mazur Conjecture
records.witness: one triple (p,E,E-prime); isogeny classes are computable
records.exactTarget: For every prime p>17 and elliptic curves E,E′ over Q, prove that an isomorphism E[p]≅E′[p] as G_Q-modules implies that E and E′ are Q-isogenous.

records.title: Zagier Conjecture on Dedekind Zeta Values
records.exactTarget: For every number field F of signature (r1,r2) and every integer k>=2, put n=r2 for even k and n=r1+r2 for odd k. There exist xi_1,...,xi_n in A_k(F) tensor Q, using the allowable-symbol group defined by Zagier--Gangl section2, such that zeta_F(k) belongs to Q^times times sqrt(abs(D_F)) pi^{k([F:Q]-n)} det(L_k(sigma_i(xi_j)))_{1<=i,j<=n}. Here L_k is the single-valued polylogarithm defined there by the Bernoulli-number combination of classical polylogarithms (imaginary part for even k, real part for odd k), extended Q-linearly to symbols. For even k take one embedding from each conjugate complex pair; for odd k also take all real embeddings. The empty determinant is1. This is existence of the determinant formula, not the stronger regulator-lattice or Bloch-group rank assertion.

records.title: Growth Rate of 3-Uniform Hypergraph Ramsey Numbers
records.exactTarget: Let r_3(t) be the least N such that every red-blue coloring of the triples of an N-element set has a monochromatic t-element set. Determine the asymptotic growth of r_3(t); in particular, prove or disprove that r_3(t) is at least 2^(2^(c t)) for some constant c>0 and all sufficiently large t.

records.title: Irrationality of Euler's Constant
records.exactTarget: Prove or disprove that Euler's constant gamma = lim_{n->infty} (1 + 1/2 + ... + 1/n - log n) = 0.5772156649... is irrational.

records.title: Exponent for the passage-time variance in two-dimensional first-passage percolation
records.exactTarget: Determine the exponent chi governing the growth of Var(T(0,n)) in two-dimensional first-passage percolation, including whether the variance has order n^(2/3).

records.title: Kaplansky's Idempotent Conjecture
records.witness: an explicit idempotent in K[G]; cf. Gardam on the unit conjecture
records.exactTarget: For every field K of arbitrary characteristic and every torsion-free group G, prove that each idempotent e in the ordinary scalar group ring K[G] is 0 or 1. Here K[G] consists of finite formal K-linear combinations of elements of G, with the group multiplication extended bilinearly, and idempotent means e^2=e. The group need not be finitely generated. This is not a claim that matrix rings over K[G], completed operator algebras or integral quandle rings have no nontrivial idempotents.

records.title: Finite Spectrum Problem
records.exactTarget: Determine whether the complement in the positive integers of every spectrum of a first-order sentence over finite structures is itself the spectrum of some first-order sentence.

records.title: Exact Unassisted Quantum Capacity of the Qubit Depolarizing Channel
records.exactTarget: For every p in [0,1], determine the exact unassisted quantum capacity Q(D_p) of the memoryless qubit channel D_p(rho)=(1-p)rho+pI/2. Capacity is the supremum of asymptotically achievable rates in qubits per channel use for quantum-information transmission with vanishing error and arbitrary block coding, without preshared entanglement or auxiliary classical communication.

records.title: Polynomial-time explicit logarithmic Ramsey graphs
records.exactTarget: Does there exist one deterministic algorithm A and constants C,c>0 such that, for every integer N>=2 given in unary, A outputs the adjacency matrix of a simple N-vertex graph in time at most O(N^c), with both its clique number and independence number at most C log_2 N? This is ordinary output-size polynomial explicitness, not poly(log N)-time adjacency queries.

records.title: Grigorchuk Gap Conjecture
records.exactTarget: For every finitely generated group G with finite generating set X, let gamma_G,X(n) count elements of word length at most n in X union X^(-1). For positive functions on positive integers, write f preceq g if some integer C>=1 satisfies f(n)<=C g(Cn) for every n>=1, and f prec g if f preceq g but not g preceq f. Prove that gamma_G,X prec exp(sqrt(n)) implies that G has polynomial growth, equivalently that G is virtually nilpotent. The growth comparison is independent of the finite generating set. It is strict comparison of growth classes, not merely an eventual numerical upper bound or non-strict domination.

records.title: Komlos Conjecture on Signing Unit Vectors with Bounded Infinity Norm
records.exactTarget: Prove that there is a universal constant c > 0 such that for every collection of vectors v_1, ..., v_n in the Euclidean unit ball B_2^d (any d, n), there exist signs epsilon_1, ..., epsilon_n in {-1,1} with || sum_i epsilon_i v_i ||_infinity <= c.

records.title: Unrestricted Linear-Circuit Lower Bound for the Discrete Fourier Transform
records.exactTarget: For each integer n>=2, let C_DFT(n) be the minimum number of steps needed to compute every output of the unnormalized complex DFT y_j=sum_(l=0)^(n-1) exp(-2*pi*i*j*l/n)x_l, 0<=j<n. Initially available functions are input coordinates and scalar constants; each step adds one affine function lambda*f+mu*g from two previously available functions with arbitrary complex scalars. Assertion: there exist c>0 and N such that C_DFT(n)>=c*n*log(n) for all n>=N. No coefficient bound, conditioning or memory restriction is imposed beyond this two-input scalar-step model.

records.title: Alperin–McKay Conjecture
records.witness: one finite group; k_0(B) is computable
records.exactTarget: For every finite group G, every prime p, every p-block B of G with defect group D, and its Brauer correspondent b in N_G(D), the numbers k_0(B) and k_0(b) of ordinary irreducible complex characters of height zero are equal. For a character chi in a p-block of a finite group H with defect group D, height zero means chi(1)_p=|H:D|_p, where a_p is the largest power of p dividing the positive integer a.

records.title: Complex linearity of closed-surface mapping class groups by genus
records.exactTarget: For every integer g >= 3, let S_g be the closed connected orientable surface of genus g and Mod(S_g) its group of isotopy classes of orientation-preserving homeomorphisms. Determine exactly the set of such genera g for which there exist an integer n >= 1 and an injective homomorphism Mod(S_g) -> GL_n(C), with n allowed to depend on g. A complete resolution proves the answer for every g >= 3; one nonlinear genus, a bounded-dimensional obstruction, or an isolated family of representations without the remaining genus answers is partial progress.

records.title: Montgomery's Large Value Conjecture for Dirichlet Polynomials
records.exactTarget: For every fixed sigma > 1/2 and N <= T <= N^{O(1)}, prove that if D(t) = sum_{N<n<=2N} b_n exp(it log n) has |b_n| <= 1 and W is a 1-separated subset of [0,T] on which |D(t)| > N^sigma, then |W| <= C(sigma) T^{o(1)} N^{2-2sigma}.

records.title: Huisken's Generic Singularity Conjecture for Mean Curvature Flow
records.exactTarget: Prove that, for a generic open dense set of smooth closed embedded initial hypersurfaces in R^(n+1), every mean-curvature-flow singularity is modeled by a multiplicity-one sphere or cylinder.

records.title: Griffiths Positivity Conjecture for Ample Vector Bundles
records.exactTarget: For every ample holomorphic vector bundle E on a smooth complex projective variety X, prove that E admits a smooth Hermitian metric h whose Chern curvature is Griffiths positive: for every point x and nonzero vectors v in T_x^(1,0)X and e in E_x, the Hermitian pairing of Theta_(E,h)(v, conjugate(v))e with e is strictly positive.

records.title: C^r Closing Lemma
records.exactTarget: For every differentiability order r, compact smooth manifold M, C^r diffeomorphism f of M, nonwandering point p, and C^r neighborhood U of f, prove that some g in U has p as a periodic point.

records.title: Bass-Quillen conjecture
records.exactTarget: Prove or disprove that for every regular ring R and every d >= 0, every vector bundle on affine d-space over R descends from R; equivalently, every finitely generated projective R[t_1,...,t_d]-module is extended from R.

records.title: Lions' Open Problem on Small-Time Global Exact Null Controllability of the Navier-Stokes Equations with Dirichlet Boundary Conditions
records.exactTarget: Let Omega be a bounded domain, Gamma a nonempty open subset of its boundary, and T > 0. For every divergence-free initial velocity u_0 in the natural L^2 phase space, does there exist boundary data f supported on Gamma and a weak solution of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with u=f on Gamma, u=0 on the uncontrolled boundary, u(0)=u_0, and u(T)=0?

records.title: Tutte 5-Flow Conjecture
records.witness: one finite bridgeless graph with no such flow
records.exactTarget: Prove that every finite bridgeless graph admits an orientation and a flow f on its edges with integer values in {-4,-3,-2,-1,1,2,3,4}, such that the sum of outgoing values equals the sum of incoming values at every vertex.

records.title: Gromov's Surface Subgroup Question for One-Ended Hyperbolic Groups
records.exactTarget: Prove that every one-ended word-hyperbolic group contains a subgroup isomorphic to the fundamental group of a closed surface of negative Euler characteristic.

records.title: Hartshorne Conjecture on complete intersections in codimension two
records.exactTarget: Prove that for every integer N >= 7, every smooth codimension-two subvariety X of complex projective space P^N is the scheme-theoretic intersection of two hypersurfaces.

records.title: Vassiliev Separation by Abelian-Valued Finite-Type Invariants
records.exactTarget: For every pair of non-isotopic smooth closed oriented unframed knots K_1,K_2 in S^3, assert that there exist an abelian group A, a nonnegative integer d and an A-valued Vassiliev invariant v of order at most d with v(K_1) != v(K_2). Knots are taken up to ambient isotopy respecting their orientation, so a knot and its reverse are included when they are distinct oriented knot types. Extend v linearly from the free abelian group on oriented knot types to singular knots by the usual alternating positive/negative crossing-resolution relation; order at most d means vanishing on every singular knot with d+1 transverse double points. The coefficient group and finite order may depend on the pair. Rational-valued, integer-valued and Kontsevich-injectivity variants are related but are not asserted equivalent here.

records.title: Slice-Ribbon Conjecture
records.witness: a knot diagram -- but "slice and not ribbon" is not decidable
records.exactTarget: Is every smoothly slice knot in S^3 (one that bounds a smoothly embedded disk in the 4-ball) a ribbon knot (one bounding an immersed disk in S^3 with only ribbon singularities)?

records.title: Alperins Weight Conjecture for Modular Representations of Finite Groups
records.witness: one finite group / block
records.exactTarget: Prove that the number of isomorphism classes of simple modules of a p-block B of a finite group G equals the number of G-conjugacy classes of B-weights.

records.title: Normality of Pi
records.exactTarget: Prove that pi is a normal number: in every integer base b >= 2, every block of k digits occurs in the base-b expansion of pi with asymptotic frequency b^{-k}.

records.title: Birkhoff Conjecture (Near-Boundary Continuous Invariant Foliation)
records.exactTarget: For every bounded planar billiard domain Omega whose boundary is a C-infinity simple closed curve with everywhere positive curvature, let T be its usual specular-reflection billiard map on the open phase cylinder M=(R/LZ) x (0,pi), where s is boundary arclength and delta is the incoming angle with the tangent. Suppose an open annular neighborhood U of the grazing end delta=0 is foliated by continuous simple closed T-invariant curves, each essential in M and winding once around the cylinder; U and its foliation are invariant under T. Here neighborhood of that end means U contains (R/LZ) x (0,eta) for some eta>0, with no fixed lower bound on eta or on the rotation numbers reached by the foliation. Assert that the boundary of Omega is an ellipse, with circles included. No central symmetry, closeness to an ellipse, period-four caustic or extension of the foliation to the whole phase cylinder is assumed. The invariant-curve formulation is selected directly; an unproved equivalence to a caustic, rational, measurable or polynomial-integral formulation is not part of the target.

records.title: Marked Length Spectrum Rigidity Conjecture
records.exactTarget: Let g and h be negatively curved Riemannian metrics on the same closed manifold. Prove that equality of their marked length spectra implies that a diffeomorphism isotopic to the identity pulls h back to g.

records.title: Woodin's HOD Conjecture
records.exactTarget: Prove or refute that ZFC plus the existence of an extendible cardinal implies there is a proper class of regular cardinals that are not omega-strongly measurable in HOD.

records.title: Finiteness of Finitely Presented Periodic Groups
records.exactTarget: Prove or disprove that every finitely presented group in which every element has finite order is finite; equivalently, decide whether an infinite finitely presented periodic group exists.

records.title: Planar homogeneous Mumford–Shah local-structure conjecture
records.exactTarget: Let Omega be any open subset of R^2. Consider every reduced absolute local minimizer (u,K) of E0(u,K;U)=integral_{U minus K}|grad u|^2 dx+H^1(K intersect U): K is relatively closed and countably 1-rectifiable, u is real and in W^{1,2}_loc(Omega minus K), E0 is finite on each relatively compact open U, and H^1(K intersect V)=0 implies K intersect V is empty for every open V contained in Omega. Absolute local minimality means E0(u,K;U)<=E0(v,J;U) for every relatively compact open U and every admissible locally finite-energy pair (v,J) for which (J symmetric-difference K) union the support of u-v is compactly contained in U; equality of functions off that compact set is understood almost everywhere on their common domain. There is no component-count or separation restriction on competitors. Must every x in K have a disk B_r(x) compactly contained in Omega and a C1 diffeomorphism Phi:B_r(x)->B_r(x), with Phi(x)=x and D Phi(x)=Id, such that Phi(K intersect B_r(x)) is one of: a diameter through x, one radius ending at x, or three radii ending at x with mutual120-degree angles?

records.title: Legendre's Conjecture on Primes Between Consecutive Squares
records.witness: one n; the inner existential is bounded, so the predicate is decidable
records.exactTarget: Prove that for every positive integer n there exists a prime p with n^2 < p < (n+1)^2.

records.title: Exact Real Grothendieck Constant
records.exactTarget: Determine the smallest real constant K_G such that, for every finite real m-by-n matrix (a_ij) and all unit vectors u_1,...,u_m,v_1,...,v_n in a real Hilbert space, abs(sum_ij a_ij <u_i,v_j>) <= K_G max_{epsilon_i,delta_j in {-1,1}} abs(sum_ij a_ij epsilon_i delta_j). The constant is uniform over both matrix sizes and Hilbert-space dimension.

records.title: Bodirsky-Pinsker Tractability Conjecture for Infinite-Domain Constraint Satisfaction
records.exactTarget: For every finite-signature first-order reduct A of a countable finitely bounded homogeneous relational structure, determine whether absence of a primitive-positive construction of the three-vertex complete graph K3 implies that CSP(A), the finite-input homomorphism problem to the fixed template A, has a polynomial-time algorithm.

records.title: Deterministic polynomial-time exact bipartite matching
records.witness: deterministic exact bipartite matching
records.exactTarget: Does there exist a deterministic algorithm which, for every explicitly encoded finite simple bipartite graph G=(U∪V,E), a red/blue colouring of E and an integer k encoded in binary, decides in time polynomial in the total input bit length whether G has a perfect matching with exactly k red edges? Unequal side sizes or k outside 0,...,|U| are immediate No instances.

records.title: Infinitude of Sophie Germain Primes
records.exactTarget: Determine whether there are infinitely many Sophie Germain primes, that is, primes p such that 2p + 1 is also prime.

records.title: Dixmier Conjecture
records.exactTarget: Let K be a field of characteristic zero and A_1(K) the first Weyl algebra. Prove that every K-algebra endomorphism of A_1(K) is an automorphism.

records.title: Iwasawa mu = 0 Conjecture for Cyclotomic Z_p-Extensions
records.exactTarget: For every number field F and every prime p, prove that the Iwasawa mu-invariant mu(X_infinity) of the unramified Iwasawa module for the cyclotomic Z_p-extension F_infinity/F is zero. The case in which F is abelian over Q is excluded as proved.

records.title: Néel Order for the Spin-1/2 Square-Lattice Heisenberg Antiferromagnet (Averaged Ground-State Order)
records.exactTarget: For each even L let H_L=sum_{<x,y>} S_x dot S_y be the nearest-neighbour isotropic spin-1/2 antiferromagnetic Heisenberg Hamiltonian on the periodic L by L square lattice, with coupling normalized to one and unique normalized ground state Phi_L. Put M_L=sum_x (-1)^(x_1+x_2) S_x^(3) and q_L=<Phi_L,(M_L/L^2)^2 Phi_L>. Assertion: liminf_{L->infinity, L even} q_L>0, equivalently there exist q>0 and L_0 such that q_L>=q for every even L>=L_0.

records.title: The Dynamic Optimality Conjecture for Splay Trees
records.exactTarget: Prove that there is a universal constant C such that, for every access sequence, the cost of the splay-tree algorithm is at most C times the minimum cost of any offline dynamic binary search tree algorithm, up to the standard additive initialization term.

records.title: Hopf Conjecture: no metric of positive sectional curvature on S^2 x S^2
records.exactTarget: Determine whether the product S^2 x S^2 admits a Riemannian metric of positive sectional curvature; the Hopf conjecture asserts that no such metric exists.

records.title: Amenability of Thompson's Group F
records.exactTarget: Determine whether Richard Thompson's group F of piecewise-linear orientation-preserving homeomorphisms of the unit interval is amenable.

records.title: Chowla Non-Vanishing Conjecture for Dirichlet L-Functions at the Central Point
records.exactTarget: For every integer q>=1 and every primitive Dirichlet character chi of conductor q, including real and nonreal characters and both even and odd parity, the analytically continued Dirichlet L-function satisfies L(1/2,chi) != 0. The conductor-one character is included with L(s,chi)=zeta(s), whose central value is already known to be nonzero; conductors with no primitive characters contribute no cases. No positivity, quantitative lower bound, effective constant or off-central zero-free region is part of the assertion.

records.title: The Atiyah Conjecture on the Integrality of L2-Betti Numbers
records.exactTarget: Prove that for every finite CW-complex X whose group G = π_1(X) is torsion-free, the L2-Betti numbers of the universal covering of X, i.e. the von Neumann dimensions of its L2-homology, are integers.

records.title: Positivity Problem for Linear Recurrence Sequences
records.exactTarget: Select arbitrary finite order k>=1, rational constant coefficients a_1,...,a_k and rational initial values u_0,...,u_(k-1), each finitely encoded in binary, with u_(n+k)=sum_(i=1)^k a_i u_(n+k-i) for all n>=0. The assertion is that a total algorithm exists which, for EVERY such input, halts and correctly decides whether u_n>=0 for EVERY n>=0. There is no running-time bound. All coefficient values, including a_k=0, are permitted.

records.title: Sinai's Positive Metric Entropy Conjecture for the Chirikov Standard Map
records.exactTarget: Prove that there is a positive-Lebesgue-measure set Lambda of parameters k for which the Chirikov standard map f_k(x,y) = (x + y + k sin(2 pi x), y + k sin(2 pi x)) mod Z^2 has positive metric entropy with respect to Lebesgue measure; equivalently, it has a positive-measure orbit set with a nonzero Lyapunov exponent.

records.title: Graph reconstruction conjecture
records.witness: two finite graphs sharing a deck
records.exactTarget: Prove or disprove that every finite simple undirected graph on at least three vertices is determined up to isomorphism by the multiset of its vertex-deleted subgraphs.

records.title: Zariski Multiplicity Conjecture for Hypersurface Singularities
records.exactTarget: For reduced holomorphic germs f,g:(C^n,0)->(C,0), prove that if the embedded hypersurface germs (V(f),0) and (V(g),0) are ambient topologically equivalent, then their multiplicities at the origin are equal; equivalently, prove that multiplicity is an invariant of embedded topological type for reduced complex analytic hypersurface singularities.

records.title: Log-Brunn-Minkowski Inequality for Symmetric Convex Bodies
records.exactTarget: Prove or disprove the conjecture of Boroczky, Lutwak, Yang and Zhang that for origin-symmetric convex bodies K and L in R^n and any lambda in [0,1], the volume of the log-convex combination satisfies |(1-lambda) K +_0 lambda L| >= |K|^(1-lambda) |L|^lambda, strengthening the Brunn-Minkowski inequality in the symmetric case.

records.title: Broues Abelian Defect Group Conjecture
records.exactTarget: Prove that if B is a p-block of a finite group G with abelian defect group D and b is the Brauer correspondent block in N_G(D), then the bounded derived categories D^b(mod B) and D^b(mod b) are equivalent as triangulated categories.

records.title: Calderón uniqueness for bounded measurable real isotropic conductivities
records.exactTarget: For every integer n>=3, every bounded connected Lipschitz domain Omega in R^n and every pair of real scalar conductivities gamma_1,gamma_2 in L-infinity(Omega) with 0<c<=gamma_j<=C<infinity almost everywhere for some constants c,C, equality Lambda_gamma_1=Lambda_gamma_2 of the full weak Dirichlet-to-Neumann operators H^(1/2)(boundary Omega)->H^(-1/2)(boundary Omega) implies gamma_1=gamma_2 almost everywhere. For trace f, u is the unique H^1 solution of div(gamma grad u)=0 with trace f, and <Lambda_gamma f,g>=integral_Omega gamma grad u dot grad v for any H^1 extension v of test trace g. No coefficient derivatives, boundary agreement, connected-complement, smallness or nonzero-frequency hypothesis is imposed.

records.title: Erdős Girth Conjecture
records.exactTarget: For every integer k>=2, there exist constants c_k>0 and N_k such that for every integer n>=N_k there is a finite simple undirected graph on n vertices with girth greater than 2k and at least c_k n^(1+1/k) edges. Forests have infinite girth. Equivalently ex(n,{C_3,...,C_(2k)})=Omega_k(n^(1+1/k)) as n tends to infinity. Constants and the threshold may depend on k; k is fixed before n grows.

records.title: Discontinuity of the q-State Potts Phase Transition on Z^d for d >= 3 and q >= 3
records.exactTarget: Prove that the order/disorder phase transition of the nearest-neighbor q-state Potts model on Z^d with d >= 3 is discontinuous (first-order) for every integer q >= 3.

records.title: Černý Conjecture on Shortest Reset Words of Synchronizing Automata
records.exactTarget: Prove or refute that every synchronizing deterministic finite automaton with n states admits a reset (synchronizing) word of length at most (n-1)^2, i.e., that the reset threshold of every n-state synchronizing automaton does not exceed (n-1)^2.

records.title: Original Dubrovin conjecture for Fano manifolds
records.exactTarget: For every smooth projective complex Fano manifold F, prove the original Dubrovin conjecture in the form recalled in Galkin-Golyshev-Iritani Section 4.6: (1) the (big) quantum cohomology of F is generically semisimple if and only if the bounded derived category D^b_coh(F) admits a full exceptional collection; and, if the quantum cohomology is semisimple (quantum product convergent and semisimple at some point tau, with the monodromy data taken at tau and an admissible phase in that paper's conventions of Sections 2 and 4.5), there exists a full exceptional collection E_1,...,E_N such that (2) the Stokes matrix satisfies S_ij = chi(E_i,E_j) for all i,j, and (3) the central connection matrix factors as C = C'C'' where the columns of C'' are the components of the modified Chern characters Ch(E_j) and C' is an operator on cohomology commuting with cup product by c_1(F). The explicit Gamma-class formula for C' (Gamma Conjecture II) and the Hodge-Tate refined versions are not part of this target.

records.title: The Hadamard Matrix Existence Conjecture
records.witness: a Hadamard matrix of order 4k; H H^T = 4k I
records.exactTarget: Prove that there exists a Hadamard matrix of order 4k for every positive integer k.

records.title: Worst-case to average-case hardness reduction for the Learning Parity with Noise problem
records.exactTarget: Decide whether average-case hardness of Learning Parity with Noise in the standard constant-noise regime can be established by a worst-case-to-average-case reduction from a worst-case decoding problem.

records.title: Irrationality of zeta(5)
records.exactTarget: Prove that zeta(5) = sum_{n>=1} 1/n^5 is irrational.

records.title: Nonlinear Landau Damping at the Sharp Gevrey Regularity Threshold for Vlasov-Poisson
records.exactTarget: Prove nonlinear Landau damping for the Vlasov-Poisson equations near homogeneous equilibria at and below the conjectured sharp Gevrey regularity threshold s = 1/3 in dimensions d > 1, including optimal stability thresholds in the perturbation size.

records.title: Jones Unknot Conjecture
records.witness: one diagram; Jones is computable and unknot recognition is decidable
records.exactTarget: Prove or disprove: a knot K in S^3 has Jones polynomial V_K = 1 if and only if K is the unknot (equivalently, every nontrivial knot has nontrivial Jones polynomial).

records.title: Positive Combinatorial Rule for Kronecker Coefficients
records.exactTarget: Find a positive combinatorial interpretation or rule for the Kronecker coefficients g_{lambda,mu,nu}, equivalently the multiplicities of irreducible symmetric-group representations indexed by nu in tensor products of those indexed by lambda and mu, for all partitions lambda, mu, and nu of n.

records.title: Capacity of the binary deletion channel
records.exactTarget: Determine the exact average-error Shannon capacity C_del(d) of the binary deletion channel for every fixed deletion probability d with 0 < d < 1.

records.title: Constant-Parameter Quantum Locally Testable Codes
records.exactTarget: Construct an infinite family of quantum locally testable codes with asymptotically constant rate, relative distance, soundness, and local-projector weight, or prove that no such family exists.

records.title: Polynomial-time unknot recognition
records.witness: polynomial-time unknot recognition
records.exactTarget: Determine whether there is a polynomial-time algorithm that, given a knot diagram or an equivalent finite encoding of a knot in three-space, decides whether the knot is the unknot.

records.title: The Online Boolean Matrix-Vector Multiplication Conjecture
records.exactTarget: Prove or refute that for every epsilon > 0 there is no randomized algorithm which, given an n by n Boolean matrix and then n Boolean query vectors one at a time, outputs each Boolean-semiring product before receiving the next vector in total time O(n^(3-epsilon)) with error probability at most 1/3.

records.title: Existence of a p-Optimal Propositional Proof System
records.exactTarget: Determine whether there exists a Cook-Reckhow propositional proof system that polynomially simulates every other propositional proof system, including a polynomial-time translation of proofs.

records.title: Arnold Chord Conjecture in Higher Dimensions
records.exactTarget: Prove that for every closed co-oriented contact manifold (Y, xi) of dimension 2n+1 with n >= 2, every contact form alpha for xi, and every closed Legendrian submanifold Lambda of Y, there exists a Reeb chord of Lambda: a non-constant trajectory of the Reeb vector field of alpha starting and ending on Lambda. Hutchings-Taubes proved the three-dimensional case (all Legendrian knots in all closed contact 3-manifolds); the conjecture is open in higher dimensions apart from special cases (subcritical Stein boundaries, conormal bundles, convex hypersurfaces).

records.title: Bott Conjecture: nonnegatively curved simply connected manifolds are rationally elliptic
records.exactTarget: Prove that every compact simply connected manifold M admitting a metric of nonnegative sectional curvature is rationally elliptic, i.e., the Betti numbers of its loop space grow at most polynomially for every field of coefficients.

records.title: Koebe circle-domain uniformization conjecture
records.exactTarget: For every nonempty connected open domain Omega of the Riemann sphere, there exist a circle domain D in the Riemann sphere and a conformal homeomorphism Omega -> D. A circle domain means a nonempty connected open set each of whose complementary components is a closed round disk or a point. Allow arbitrary connectivity, including uncountably many complementary components and point components; the whole sphere (empty complement) and a sphere minus one point are included as trivial circle-domain cases. Conformal homeomorphism means a bijective conformal map, not a possibly noninjective holomorphic covering. No uniqueness, Mobius rigidity, quantitative distortion, explicit construction or boundary-extension requirement is appended. The universal statement is retained, not replaced by only an uncountable-connectivity or otherwise difficult subclass.

records.title: Erdos-Szekeres Convex Polygon Problem (Happy Ending Problem)
records.witness: 2^(n-2)+1 points in general position with no n in convex position
records.exactTarget: Determine the exact least integer ES(n) such that every set of ES(n) points in general position in the plane contains n points in convex position; prove or disprove ES(n)=2^(n-2)+1 for every n >= 3.

records.title: Corona problem for the unit polydisc
records.exactTarget: For every integer n>=2 and every finite integer m>=1, let f_1,...,f_m be scalar bounded holomorphic functions on the unit polydisc D^n={z in C^n: |z_k|<1 for all k}. If inf_{z in D^n} sum_{j=1}^m |f_j(z)|>0, then there exist scalar bounded holomorphic g_1,...,g_m on D^n such that sum_{j=1}^m f_j g_j=1 identically. No boundary extension, regularity, operator inequality or sharp solution-norm bound is required. Equivalently, for every n>=2, point evaluations from D^n are dense in the maximal ideal space of H-infinity(D^n).

records.title: Arithmeticity of Lattices in PU(n,1) for n at Least 4
records.exactTarget: For every integer n>=4, every lattice Γ in PU(n,1), the group of holomorphic isometries of complex hyperbolic n-space, is arithmetic. A lattice is a discrete subgroup of finite Haar covolume; both compact and noncompact finite-volume quotients and groups with torsion are included. Arithmeticity has its usual commensurability meaning via arithmetic subgroups of algebraic groups over Q projected through a compact-kernel real-group homomorphism, equivalently after the finite central lift to SU(n,1). No restriction to reflection lattices or one particular arithmetic construction is imposed. Here n is complex dimension, not real rank.

records.title: Beal's Conjecture (Tijdeman-Zagier Conjecture)
records.witness: one 6-tuple A^x+B^y=C^z with A,B,C coprime
records.exactTarget: Prove that if A^x + B^y = C^z with A, B, C, x, y, z positive integers and x, y, z all greater than 2, then A, B, and C have a common prime factor.

records.title: Coding Theory and Combinatorics Problem CC-8: Exact Kissing Numbers in Higher Dimensions n > 4
records.exactTarget: For each dimension n > 4, determine the kissing number tau_n, the maximum number of pairwise nonoverlapping unit n-spheres that can simultaneously touch one central unit n-sphere.

records.title: Iwaniec Conjecture for the Beurling-Ahlfors Transform Norm
records.exactTarget: For every 1<p<infinity, prove or disprove that the Beurling-Ahlfors transform B on complex-valued L^p(C) has operator norm ||B||_p=p^*-1, where p^*=max(p,p/(p-1)).

records.title: Exact Capacity Region of the Two-User Gaussian Interference Channel
records.exactTarget: Determine the exact capacity region of the two-user Gaussian interference channel in the moderately weak and strong interference regimes.

records.title: Beck-Fiala Conjecture
records.exactTarget: Prove that there is a universal constant C such that every hypergraph H in which each vertex lies in at most t edges has discrepancy at most C sqrt(t).

records.title: Asymptotic Turan Numbers of Even Cycles
records.exactTarget: Determine the order of magnitude of ex(n, C_{2k}), the maximum number of edges in an n-vertex graph with no cycle of length 2k, for every fixed k.

records.title: The Word Problem for One-Relation Monoids
records.exactTarget: Determine whether every monoid defined by a single defining relation has a solvable word problem: given a one-relation monoid presentation <a_1, ..., a_n | u = v> and two words over the generators, decide whether the two words represent the same element of the monoid; no undecidable one-relation monoid is known and no algorithm solving the general case is known.

records.title: Tutte's 3-Flow Conjecture
records.witness: one 4-edge-connected multigraph with no nowhere-zero 3-flow
records.exactTarget: Every finite loopless multigraph G that is 4-edge-connected admits a nowhere-zero integer 3-flow: there exist an orientation D of E(G) and a function f:E(G)->{-2,-1,1,2} such that at each vertex the sum of f on incoming edges equals the sum on outgoing edges. Four-edge-connected means G remains connected after deletion of any set of at most3 edges. Parallel edges are allowed. Trivial one-vertex loopless graphs have the empty flow. This is the ordinary zero-boundary flow assertion, not the stronger claim of realizing every admissible prescribed boundary modulo3.

records.title: Brauer's k(B) Conjecture
records.witness: one finite group with k(B) > |D|
records.exactTarget: For every finite group G, every prime p, and every p-block B of G with defect group D, prove that k(B)=|Irr(B)|, the number of ordinary complex irreducible characters belonging to B, satisfies k(B)<=|D|.

records.title: Strong Compactness versus Supercompactness Equiconsistency Problem
records.exactTarget: Determine whether Con(ZFC plus the existence of a strongly compact cardinal) implies Con(ZFC plus the existence of a supercompact cardinal), or prove that the latter has strictly greater consistency strength.

records.title: Benjamini-Schramm conjecture p_c<p_u for non-amenable Cayley graphs
records.exactTarget: Prove or disprove the Benjamini-Schramm conjecture that for any Cayley graph G of a finitely generated infinite group, p_c(G)<p_u(G) if and only if the group is non-amenable, where p_c is the percolation threshold and p_u the threshold for a unique infinite cluster.

records.title: Mazur's Conjecture on the Real Topology of Rational Points
records.exactTarget: For every algebraic variety V over Q, prove or disprove that the closure of V(Q) in V(R), with the Euclidean topology, has finitely many connected components.

records.title: Gromov's Filling Area Conjecture
records.exactTarget: For every compact orientable Riemannian surface M whose boundary is isometric to a circle C of circumference 2π and satisfies d_M(x,y)=d_C(x,y) for all x,y in C, prove Area(M) is at least 2π.

records.title: Nagata Conjecture on Plane Curve Linear Systems
records.exactTarget: Prove that for any r >= 10 very general points in the complex projective plane P^2 and nonnegative integer multiplicities m_1 through m_r, every plane curve of degree d having multiplicity at least m_i at the i-th point satisfies d > (1 / sqrt{r}) sum_{i=1}^r m_i.

records.title: Fujita Freeness Conjecture
records.exactTarget: For every smooth complex projective variety X of dimension n and every ample divisor L, prove that K_X + (n+1)L is basepoint-free.

records.title: Four Exponentials Conjecture
records.exactTarget: Prove or disprove that, for complex numbers x1, x2 linearly independent over Q and y1, y2 linearly independent over Q, at least one of the four numbers exp(x_i y_j) (i, j in {1,2}) is transcendental.

records.title: Congruence Subgroup Property for Mapping Class Groups of Surfaces of Genus at Least Three
records.exactTarget: For every closed connected orientable surface S of genus g≥3 and every finite-index subgroup H of its orientation-preserving mapping class group Mod(S), there exists a finite-index characteristic subgroup N of π1(S) such that ker(Mod(S)→Out(π1(S)/N)) is contained in H.

records.title: Hilbert's Third Problem for Spherical and Hyperbolic Scissors Congruence
records.exactTarget: Prove or disprove Dehn invariant sufficiency in spherical and hyperbolic three-dimensional geometry: for X equal to H^3 and S^3, show whether volume is injective on the kernel of the Dehn invariant, equivalently whether volume together with Dehn invariant classifies polyhedra up to scissors congruence in those geometries.

records.title: Turan Conjecture on the Turan Density of K_4^{(3)}
records.exactTarget: Prove or refute that the Turan density of the complete 3-uniform hypergraph K_4^(3) on four vertices is 5/9.

records.title: Vinogradov Conjecture on the Least Quadratic Non-Residue
records.exactTarget: Let n_p denote the least quadratic non-residue modulo an odd prime p. Prove unconditionally that for every eps > 0 one has n_p <<_eps p^eps.

records.title: Thomson problem
records.exactTarget: For each positive integer N, determine the configuration of N equal point charges on the unit sphere that minimizes total Coulomb energy.

records.title: Ivrii conjecture on periodic billiard orbits
records.exactTarget: For every integer n>=2 and every bounded connected open domain Ω in Euclidean R^n with C∞ boundary, prove the following assertion; neither convexity nor simple connectivity is assumed. Let M=B*∂Ω={(x,η) in T*∂Ω: |η|<1}, with the norm induced by the Euclidean metric and canonical symplectic (Liouville) volume μ=|ω^(n-1)|/(n-1)!, where ω is the canonical symplectic form. The billiard map β lifts (x,η) to the inward-pointing unit covector, follows the straight segment to its first subsequent boundary collision, and applies specular reflection, recording the tangential covector at that collision. Let M_reg be the set on which every forward and backward iterate is well-defined and nongrazing. For P=union over integers k>=2 of {z in M_reg: β^k(z)=z}, prove μ(P)=0. The integer k need not be the least period. Grazing collisions and any undefined singular continuation are excluded from M_reg; no rule continuing through them is imposed.

records.title: Corona Problem for the Unit Ball in Several Complex Variables
records.exactTarget: For every n ≥ 2, if f_1,...,f_m are bounded holomorphic functions on the unit ball B^n in C^n and inf_{z∈B^n} sum_j |f_j(z)| > 0, prove or disprove that there exist bounded holomorphic g_1,...,g_m on B^n with sum_j f_j g_j = 1.

records.title: Clemens Conjecture for Rational Curves on a General Quintic Threefold
records.exactTarget: Prove that a general smooth quintic threefold in complex projective four-space contains only finitely many smooth rational curves of each fixed positive degree, with the expected normal-bundle rigidity.

records.title: Whitehead Asphericity Conjecture
records.exactTarget: Decide whether every connected subcomplex of an aspherical two-dimensional CW-complex is aspherical, equivalently whether every subpresentation of an aspherical presentation is aspherical.

records.title: Serres Positivity Conjecture for Intersection Multiplicities over Regular Local Rings
records.exactTarget: For every regular local ring R and finitely generated R-modules M and N with finite length M tensor_R N and dim(M)+dim(N)=dim(R), prove that chi^R(M,N)=sum_i (-1)^i length(Tor_i^R(M,N)) is strictly positive.

records.title: Dixmier unitarisability problem for discrete groups
records.exactTarget: Every unitarisable discrete group G is amenable. Here unitarisable means: for every complex Hilbert space H and every group representation pi:G->GL(H) by bounded invertible linear operators with sup_{g in G} ||pi(g)||<infinity in operator norm, there exists a bounded invertible S on H such that S pi(g) S^{-1} is unitary for all g. There is no countability or Hilbert-space separability restriction. Equivalently, every nonamenable discrete group admits at least one uniformly bounded Hilbert-space representation not similar to a unitary one.

records.title: Sharp asymptotic order of minimal star discrepancy in each dimension d >= 3
records.exactTarget: For every fixed integer d >= 3, determine the asymptotic order, up to positive multiplicative constants depending only on d, of Delta_d(N)=inf_{P subset [0,1)^d, |P|=N} sup_{x in [0,1]^d} |#(P intersect product_j[0,x_j))-N product_j x_j| as N tends to infinity.

records.title: Kobayashi Conjecture: Hyperbolic Compact Kähler Manifolds Have Ample Canonical Bundle
records.exactTarget: For every compact connected Kähler complex manifold X that is Kobayashi hyperbolic, equivalently every holomorphic map C -> X is constant, the canonical line bundle K_X is ample.

records.title: Margulis Bounded Diagonal-Orbit Conjecture
records.exactTarget: Let A be the diagonal subgroup of SL(3,R). Prove or disprove that every bounded A-orbit in the homogeneous space SL(3,R)/SL(3,Z) is closed.

records.title: Global Regularity of the 3D Incompressible Hall-MHD Equations for Large Data
records.exactTarget: Prove or disprove that smooth solutions to the three-dimensional incompressible Hall-magnetohydrodynamics system exist globally in time for large (non-small) initial data. Known results provide local well-posedness for large data in critical spaces together with continuation criteria, and global well-posedness only under smallness assumptions on the initial data.

records.title: Toms–Winter: Strict Comparison Implies Z-Stability
records.exactTarget: For every separable, simple, nuclear, non-elementary C*-algebra A, unital or nonunital, assert that strict comparison of positive elements implies A is isomorphic to A tensor_min Z, where Z is the Jiang–Su algebra. Non-elementary excludes algebras of compact operators. In the Cuntz semigroup Cu(A) of positive elements of A tensor K modulo Cuntz equivalence, strict comparison means: x≤y whenever phi(x)≤phi(y) for every ordered-semigroup functional phi:Cu(A)→[0,infinity] preserving zero and increasing sequential suprema, with strict inequality for every such phi for which 0<phi(y)<infinity.
